dataset_role: spatiotemporal + kinematic reference for young adults (18-35 years), Asian anthropometry
source: Yu JS, Zhuang C, Guo WX, et al. (2023). Reference values of gait parameters in healthy Chinese university students: A cross-sectional observational study. World J Clin Cases, 11(29), 7061-7074.
population: Han Chinese university students; 18-35 years; BMI 18.5-23.9
device: Qualisys Track Manager 3D motion capture (8x Oqus700+, 1100 Hz) + 4x Kistler 9260AA force plates
model: Calibrated Anatomical System Technique (Cappozzo 1995); 32 reflective markers
protocol: Habitual walking pace, preferred speed, 3 best gait cycles averaged; full SPM analysis on 0-100% cycle

parameters_spatiotemporal.label: Height-adjusted cadence (note: height in m, not cm as in Yishun)

unit_warning: Yu et al. report length in METERS (m) and speed in m/s, whereas Yishun reports in CM and cm/s. When cross-comparing or feeding into a unified pipeline, convert with: gait_speed_cm_per_s = gait_speed_m_per_s * 100; step_length_cm = step_length_m * 100.
stance_swing_unit_note: Source paper reports stance/swing as FRACTION of gait cycle (e.g. 0.65); stored here multiplied by 100 (pct) for consistency with Yishun. SD values also multiplied by 100. Stance + swing > 100 because of double support overlap (per single leg).
kinematics_limitation: The source paper presents kinematics as SPM curves (figures), not scalar peak/mean/sd values. The kinematics_regions.csv documents only the *regions of statistically significant sex difference* found via SPM, NOT the underlying mean/sd curves needed for Z-score. For waveform comparison, use ntu_output/ instead.
applicability_in_project: Use this dataset for patients aged 18-35 only. For age 50-80 patients, NTU dataset is the better kinematics reference. For habitual spatiotemporal across all ages, Yishun Study is primary.
